Figure 2:Overview ofGame2Player.The Scout selects games from web portals (top).
In the co-development loop (middle), the Builder turns each game into an environment with state-verified tasks, the VLM Player and the Coding Player play every task and report faults of the game, and the Builder checks each report against the recording before repairing it.
Both players then record gameplay in the accepted environments to trainGame2Playerwith progress-weighted SFT (bottom).

Figure 3:Two players on the same task and one training format.The code policy reads the player observationψ\psiand sends keys at every frame without calling a model (top).
The VLM Player sees only the screenshot and pauses the game to choose each action (bottom).
The code policy’s keys are cut into steps in the VLM Player’s format, so both players yield the same kind of training example (middle).

Figure 11:Qwen3.5-4B and Game2Player-4B on four held-outPlayerBenchtasks, with thinking on and at most 100 steps. Each panel shows the final frame of each model with its final progress, and the best progress reached after each step.

Figure 22:A VLM Player and a code policy on the same task.In each game, the upper row shows four steps of an episode of Claude Haiku 5.5 with the screenshot it saw, its action and its note, and the lower row four moments of a code policy episode that completes the task, each at a key press or click, with the frame, the keys held and fields of the policy’s observation. Pointers mark clicks. The bar andppgive the progress the VLM Player reaches.

Figure 23:Base and trained models on held-outPlayerBenchtasks, with thinking on and at most 100 steps. Each row shows the task, the initial frame and the final frames of Qwen3.5-4B and Game2Player-4B. The curves show the best progress reached after each step.
